maria: Quick heads up — vuln scanner flagged outbound sidecar traffic to 169.254.169.254 in a customer on-prem cluster (customer: argus). Need an access review: who can reach keystores / KMS from that tenant? Also want audit checks for any decrypts in the last 24h. cc @devsec @aj :eyes:

aj: Can you paste the pod labels / sidecar image? First quick mitigation: apply a NetworkPolicy that denies egress to the link-local IP range for the affected namespace. Example: ```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-metadata-egress
  namespace: argus-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
    - to:
        - ipBlock:
            cidr: 169.254.0.0/16
      ports: []
```
This blocks cluster-level egress to metadata. Also recommend a host-level iptables short-term: `iptables -I OUTPUT -d 169.254.169.254 -j DROP` on nodes that host affected pods.

devsec: Important: we need KMS audit logs (who used KeyID: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:...:key/abc123?) — check decrypt/GenerateDataKey calls. If any decrypts line up with the suspicious timeframe, treat as potential exposure and rotate. Query example for our SIEM (pseudo): `index=kms_logs action=Decrypt keyId=abc123 | stats count by srcPod, user, timestamp`

jon: Also check kube-audit and kubelet logs for `exec` or `proxy` calls from the sidecar. Quick Splunk/KQL example: `k8s_audit where verb="create" and requestURI contains "proxy" and userAgent contains"curl"` or `json | where message contains "169.254.169.254"`.

ellie: I can rotate the ephemeral credentials and push a canary after we lock egress. Suggest rotating the service-account tokens first and re-issuing short-lived keys. I'll do it if we agree on a maintenance window — currently prefer immediate for this customer (low traffic). :lock:

maria: Pasting a snippet from the sidecar stdout (sanitized): ```
[2023-11-02T14:10:02Z] INFO curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/role-name -> 200
[2023-11-02T14:10:02Z] INFO got: {
  "Code": "Success",
  "LastUpdated": "2023-11-02T14:10:02Z"
}
```
This shows token retrieval succeeded at 14:10 UTC. Need to validate whether those creds were used to call KMS.

devsec: FYI the recent sidecar release (v2.3.1) included a change to the iptables setup that accidentally left container egress permissive when using hostNetwork:false + hostPorts. If that matches the cluster config, we should pin sidecar to previous image and open a PR to revert the change. Capture the image digest for rollback.

aj: Quick mitigation checklist I ran locally: `kubectl -n argus-namespace apply -f deny-metadata-egress.yaml` then `kubectl get networkpolicy -n argus-namespace` to confirm. If CNI doesn't honor policy for hostNetwork pods, you'll need node-level firewall rules.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-20231102-argus-meta-egress. Severity: P2. Assigned: devsec, ellie. Related runbook: private-deploy-egress-response.

jon: From SIEM: query shows 3 Decrypt calls at 14:11–14:14 UTC from principal `system:serviceaccount:argus-namespace:argus-sidecar-sa`. We need full payloads / request IDs to cross-check with KMS. If confirmed, rotate the key and revoke the principal immediately.

ellie: Rotation started — revoking the SA token, issuing new one, and rotating the ephemeral key pairing. Will run the canary after config propagates. ETA ~7m.

ellie: Can confirm: post-rotation canary fails to retrieve metadata (expected). `curl --connect-timeout 1 http://169.254.169.254/latest` -> connection timed out. Good.

maria: Thanks. Can we capture a short timeline for postmortem? My notes: 14:09 vuln scan detected; 14:10 token fetch observed; 14:11-14:14 KMS decrypts; 14:20 networkpolicy applied; 14:28 key rotation done; 14:36 canary blocked. I'll open a follow-up postmortem and link the artifacts (kube-audit, sidecar logs, KMS request IDs).

devsec: Add action items: 1) Revert sidecar iptables regression and release v2.3.2. 2) Harden CI to run an egress regression test (simulate metadata access). 3) Add KMS alert rule for Decrypt spikes from non-expected principals. 4) Add automated networkpolicy for private deployments to deny link-local egress by default.

maria: Agreed. Thanks everyone. I'll attach logs to INC-20231102-argus-meta-egress and schedule a 30min postmortem tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
